title: Cross-Tenant Privilege Usage Correlator & Retention Policy Enforcer
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Our compliance and audit teams need a deterministic, tenant-scoped record of privileged role use and related identity lifecycle events (SSO/SAML sign-ins, SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning) that is residency-aware and retains evidence according to tenant retention settings. Current logs are spread across systems (Auth logs, SCIM deltas, runtime access grants) and require manual correlation for periodic access reviews and attestation artifacts.

Goal: Build a service that correlates privilege usage and identity change events across tenants, applies tenant retention/residency rules, produces signed evidence bundles for audits, and enforces retention policies by pruning or archiving records per tenant policy. The feature should integrate with existing SCIM reconciliation, SSO audit stream, and the evidence export pipeline.

Out-of-scope: Full UI for reviewers (we will expose artifacts via existing evidence export endpoints and Console links). Deep analytics/ML-driven anomaly detection (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests SSO/SAML sign-in events and SCIM provisioning/deprovisioning deltas for all tenants into a normalized event stream (timestamp, tenant_id, subject, action, source) within SLA (<= 30s for hosted events).

Privilege usage correlator can join runtime grant events (role assignments, temporary elevated sessions) with identity events and emit tenant-scoped records that include residency tag and retention TTL.

Evidence bundles: for any requested date range, the system can produce a signed NDJSON bundle (events + provenance metadata) and a CSV summary suitable for compliance requests. Bundles include KMS signature reference and export job id.

Retention policy enforcer evaluates tenant retention settings (retention_days, archive_destination, residency_requirement) and either deletes, archives to tenant-specified bucket, or marks records immutable per policy. A dry-run mode is available for the first rollout.

Automated periodic-review hooks: system produces weekly access-review payloads (list of privileged subjects, last-used timestamps, justification fields) consumable by the existing periodic access review workflow.
Monitoring/alerts: SLOs for event ingestion and export generation are instrumented in Console; alert runbooks added for failures >5% over 1h.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight correlator service subscribes to existing auth audit stream + SCIM delta queue, writes normalized events to a tenant-partitioned eventstore (topic per residency/region).
Use residency metadata present on tenant configuration to ensure events are stored and exported from correct region/partition to satisfy data residency requirements.

Retention engine runs as a scheduled worker with safe-delete semantics: 1) compute candidate records by TTL, 2) if archive_destination exists, package and push signed archive, 3) emit deletion-commit event with proof, 4) async GC of blobs.
Egress: evidence bundles are signed using KMS (HSM-backed key) and include manifest.json with checksums and provenance headers (generated_by, job_id, tenant_residency).
SCIM integrations: ingest full and incremental deltas; correlate SCIM 'deprovision' with access grant removal events to flag timebound entitlements in review payloads.
Idempotency & replay: events include source_sequence_id to allow replay and dedupe; provide a reconciliation API to rebuild tenant event indexes from raw audit sources.
test_plan: Unit tests for correlator join logic with mocked auth and SCIM events (coverage >= 90% for core join paths).
Integration test environment seeds tenants with differing residency settings and verifies exported bundle residency header and retention behavior.
E2E test: create a temporary privileged session, revoke via SCIM deprovision, run retention worker in dry-run and verify candidate list, then run enforcement and confirm archive+deletion.
Performance test: ingest sustained 200 req/s auth events and confirm correlate latency under 30s for 95th percentile.
Security test: validate KMS signing flows and ensure only authorized service principals can request evidence exports.
